title: Downtown Wyndham Street and St. George's Square construction plan
subtitle: Also: Memorial Cup bid funding, accessible ramps referral, and photo-enforcement penalty system change.
overview: The committee recommended approval of the first phase of downtown infrastructure renewal on Wyndham Street North, including the construction schedule, extended working hours, a business mitigation plan and a concept for St. George's Square. Staff said the aging pipes and roads need replacing and that tendering this fall is key to finishing by late 2027. Councillors added encouragement for a flexible, heritage-minded square design, and asked for sidewalks to be raised where possible to improve front-door access.

The committee also recommended a one-time $600,000 grant and up to $100,000 in in-kind Sleeman Centre costs toward the Guelph Storm's 2027 Memorial Cup bid, paid from the Municipal Accommodation Tax reserve only if the bid succeeds {{vote:m18}}. Staff noted this would use up that reserve until 2030.

It recommended moving speed camera and red light camera violations to an administrative penalty system around January 1, 2026. A motion on temporary accessible ramps was referred to the July Council meeting. After a closed session, the mayor reported that council received information and gave staff direction on a paramedic station lease, a back-office review and a development charges complaint. All of these go to Council for a final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended moving Automated Speed Enforcement and Red Light Camera violations to an administrative penalty system on or about January 1, 2026, with a new by-law and related agreements.
The committee referred the proposal for a three-year temporary ramp project to the July 2025 Council meeting, so staff and the absent mover could weigh in.
The committee recommended approving the 2025 Downtown Infrastructure Renewal Program Capital Implementation Plan {{vote:m11}}.
The committee recommended approving the Phase 1 sequencing plan, including extended working hours {{vote:m12}}.

The committee recommended approving the square's concept plan, with staff encouraged to keep the design flexible for patios and events and to use more natural, heritage-inspired materials {{vote:m13}}.
The committee recommended approving the mitigation plan for Phase 1 of the Wyndham Street North reconstruction {{vote:m14}}.
The committee recommended delegating authority to adjust patio parking stall, downtown hourly parking and encroachment fees during the program, with lost revenue covered by the mitigation budget.
The committee recommended a $600,000 grant and up to $100,000 in in-kind facility costs, funded from the accommodation tax reserve and contingent on winning the 2027 bid {{vote:m18}}.

debate: On accessible ramps, a delegate argued landlords, not businesses or taxpayers, are legally responsible for accessibility and urged a revised motion in September. Another delegate wanted temporary ramps available immediately and said the city's accessibility plan is too weak. Councillors raised legal and liability questions, and staff said a September referral would make budget timelines tight.

Downtown business delegates criticized the St. George's Square concept as generic. They objected to a playground and a washroom in front of retail, and wanted existing patios and flexible event space protected. They were split on whether to move the Family Fountain. Staff said the washroom follows earlier council direction, the playground reflects community input, and the design remains flexible at the detailed stage.

Staff said the schedule cannot move: the infrastructure is past due and delays would add cost. Some councillors asked about pushing work past the 2027 bicentennial or avoiding the square. Staff said that would require premium payments to the contractor. One councillor said a year's delay could be considered.

On the design amendments, one councillor wanted staff directed to build in flexibility; others preferred 'encouraged' to leave room for public input, and the change carried {{vote:m8}}. Staff said they would take either wording seriously.

On the Memorial Cup bid, councillors asked about using the whole accommodation tax reserve until 2030, a competing regional bid, and downtown construction during the event. Staff said no money is spent unless the bid succeeds. Supporters cited economic benefit, while the chair said the Storm should answer questions when the matter returns to Council.
